name: Interest-Rate-Driven Early Exercise of a Deep ITM Long Put
summary: A decision rule rather than a position: exercise a long deep-in-the-money put early, against shares already held, when the interest earnable on the strike proceeds exceeds the put's remaining extrinsic value - the interest-rate counterpart to the bank's dividend arbitrage.

legs.strike_rule: 100 shares already held (the put must be exercised against shares, never naked - exercising without shares creates a short position)
an existing long put with |delta| >= 0.95 and strike well above spot, from a married put, protective put or collar already on the books

max_profit: The interest earned on (strike x 100) between the exercise date and expiry, minus the extrinsic value surrendered - typically tens of dollars per contract, and larger the higher rates are and the deeper the put is
max_loss: The forfeited extrinsic value plus the upside given up if the shares rally after the early sale - which is why the delta and extrinsic thresholds must both be met
breakevens: Exercise is correct when: strike x 100 x r x (days to expiry / 365) > put extrinsic x 100, with r the current risk-free rate

greeks.delta: the exercise converts a -0.95+ delta put plus +1.00 delta shares into flat cash
greeks.theta: the surrendered extrinsic is precisely what the decision weighs

typical_dte: Applies most often at 7-45 DTE on puts that are 15%+ in the money
when_to_use: Whenever the account holds a deep ITM long put against shares. The rule should run daily as a scan over existing positions, not be traded into deliberately - the bank's dividend arbitrage entry answers 'when do I get assigned early on a short call'; this answers 'when should I exercise my own long put'.
entry_rules: This is a position-management rule. It creates no new position and requires no new order beyond the exercise instruction.
SCAN DAILY over all long puts held: flag any with |delta| >= 0.95 AND extrinsic value < strike x r x (DTE/365), where r is the current 3-month T-bill yield.
MANDATORY PRECONDITION: the account must hold >= 100 shares per contract to be exercised. Exercising a long put without shares creates a 100-share SHORT position, which this system must never do.

Compare against the alternative: selling the put and selling the shares separately in the market. If that combination nets more after spreads and commissions, do that instead and skip the exercise - usually true when the put's bid/ask is tight.
Do not exercise if an ex-dividend date falls before expiry and the shares are held for the dividend - holding the shares to capture it may beat the interest.
Submit the exercise through Alpaca's exercise endpoint before the broker's cutoff (typically 17:30 ET, but use the broker's stated time minus a 60-minute safety margin).
management_rules: Re-run the scan every session at 14:30 ET so there is time to act before the cutoff.
Recompute with the live T-bill yield, not a hard-coded rate - the rule is worthless at 0% rates and material at 5%.
Log every exercise with the extrinsic forfeited and the interest captured, so the rule can be audited for whether it is actually adding value.
After the exercise, the shares are gone: cancel any covered call or other overlay that depended on them in the same session.
exit_rules: The exercise IS the exit for both legs simultaneously - shares sold at the strike, put extinguished.
Never exercise into a position the account cannot hold; verify share count programmatically immediately before submitting.
If the exercise instruction fails or is rejected, close the put and sell the shares in the market before the close rather than carrying an unresolved state overnight.
Never exercise on the final trading day as a substitute for closing - at that point the interest captured is a single night and the operational risk dominates.
assignment_risk: None created by this rule - it exercises the account's own long option. The related risk it does create is downstream: any short call written against those shares becomes uncovered the instant the shares are delivered away, so overlays must be cancelled in the same session.
buying_power: Frees capital: the shares convert to cash at the strike.
liquidity_needs: None for the exercise itself; the comparison against a market close does need a quotable put.
common_mistakes: Exercising a long put with no shares behind it and creating a short stock position; using a stale interest rate; ignoring a covered call still written against the shares; exercising when simply selling both legs in the market would net more.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - with hours left there is no interest to capture.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
